Issue body actions

Hello there,

I currently have a FreeNAS setup with a jail for Sonarr that works beautifully. I am trying to add a custom jail to house the Jackett application to complement it for trackers I use (TorrentDay, TorrentLeech, TV Chaos UK).

I have followed steps for the setup of the jail/Jackett app via instructions found on post 24 on the following site:

[https://forums.freenas.org/index.php?threads/need-help-installing-jackett-on-freenas-in-a-jail.38384/](https://forums.freenas.org/index.php?threads/need-help-installing-jackett-on-freenas-in-a-jail.38384/)

I've also posted by findings on post 25/26 to see if anyone else using FreeNAS is experiencing the issue.

In a nutshell, when I setup Jackett it only seems to be partially working. Torrentleech is working as expected, but TorrentDay constantly fails when trying to add the tracker citing cookie issues. TV Chaos UK just simply needs a username and password but also just doesn't work at all. I do get an error in the console for trying to add TorrentDay which is the following, but generally don't see much else to go off of in terms of errors:

```
# service jackett start

```

It also seems that the API key Jackett creates (in the upper right-hand corner of the page) seems to 'reset' upon each reboot of the jail / system.

This all contrasted to a test Windows setup I tried and everything seems to run smoothly there.

Has anyone gotten Jackett to successfully run in a FreeNAS jail or know what could be causing my issues?

The log line "Debug UnixLibCurlWebClient:GetString Returning InternalServerError =>" from your initial log actually indicates a TLS issue (missing certificates or incompatible algorithms in your openssl version).

What's the output of `curl -v https://tdonline.org/browse.php` (run it from your jail)?

Make sure you're using an up to date version of Jackett as it also fixes some cookie handling issues.

For TorrentDay just using the cookies from any IP (no need for a tunnel) should work. For BeyondHD the login has been changed to their login link method which should work independently of local/remote access too.

I also started a wiki article ( [https://github.com/Jackett/Jackett/wiki/Remote-access-via-proxy](https://github.com/Jackett/Jackett/wiki/Remote-access-via-proxy)) showing how to access a remote jackett installation via 127.0.0.1
